Ltd on 7 October, 2013 In The Court Of Shri Arun Bhardwaj Presiding Officer:Motor Accident Claims Tribunalii, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi Mact No. 200/11/10 In The Matter Of : Shri Raja Ram Yadav, S/o Shri Yadram Yadav, Smq126/11, Old Pinto Park, Air Force Palam, New Delhi - 10. Versus 1. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., (Bus Insurer) 5th Floor, Jeevan Tara Building, New Delhi - 110 001. And also at: 304, 3rd Floor Bhandari House, Nehru Place, New Delhi. Also at: TejpurBranch, Distt. Sonitpur, Nero Guwahati(Assam) - 781 005. 2. Shri Suresh Sarup, (Bus Owner) S/o Late Shri Puranmal, Saral Village B.R. Road, Tezpur, Distt. Sonitpur (Assam). 3. Shri Mahendra Barmahalia, (Bus Driver) S/o Shri Barmahtia, Vill. Bargaon, Bata More, Sonitpur (Assam). ... R Mact No.200/11/10 Shri Raja Ram Yadav Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Ors Filed On : 17.04.2010 Reserved On : 25.09.2013 Decided On : 07.10.2013 J U D G M E N T :
texts.facts: This claim petition is filed under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for grant of compensation. 2. Respondent No. 1 is the insurer, Respondent No. 2 is the owner and Respondent No. 3 is the driver of the offending vehicle. 3. It is stated in this claim petition that on 24.06.2006, the claimant was travelling with his colleagues in the Bus bearing Registration No. AS12/3611 under Assam State Road Transport Corporation but the bus turned turtle and the leg of the claimant was trapped resulting in Right Leg below Knee Amputation, Open Fracture Right Femur, Open Left Metatarsal Laceration Foot and Permanent Disability. 4. Claimant has stated that FIR No. 199/06 was registered under Section 279/337 and 338 of IPC at Police Station Dalgaon, Assam. 5. Claimant has stated that he remained hospitalized for about seven months and incurred nearly Rs. 5,50,000/ on his treatment, special diet, post care operation etc. 6. Claimant has stated that at the time of accident, his age was 38 years and he was working as a Sergeant in Indian Air Force at a salary of Rs. 20,000/ per month. 7. Claimant has stated that the accident was caused by Respondent No. 3 while driving the offending vehicle rashly and negligently. 8. Claimant has stated that before this accident, he was physically fit but now after amputation of his leg, he is declared medically unfit and is kept in Medical Category 'C' (A4G4) and earlier his Medical Category was 'A' (A4G1). 9. Claimant has stated that at least he would have been promoted upto the rank of Master Warrant Officer. However, due to accidental injuries, his promotional avenues were shuttered down. He has claimed a compensation of Rs. 32,19,941/ towards difference in the salary drawn by him today and the salary he may have drawn after promotion, if he had not suffered with accidental injuries. 10. Claimant has also stated that he was a Post Graduate with first division in English literature having a great chances to become a Commissioned Officer in the Indian Air Force and may have reached upto the rank of Group Captain in the normal procedure adopted for promotions. 11. Claimant has stated that he was pursuing MBA from IGNOU and the validity of entrance test was upto September, 2006 but during that period he was hospitalized due to accidental injuries. 12. Claimant has further stated that the studies of his two daughters were disrupted due to this accident and in case, he is discharged from his service due to this accident, it will be extremely Shri Raja Ram Yadav vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 7 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54118099/ 2 difficult for him to provide education to his daughters. He has stated that after the accident, he had shifted from Assam and he had to get his daughters admitted in a public school at his native place as they could not get admission in Kendriya Vidayala school constraining him to face additional financial burden. He has also stated that his family had to immediately fly to Assam after hearing the news of his accident incurring extra expenses. 13. Therefore, the claimant has claimed a compensation of Rs. 37,69,941/ from the respondents. 14. Respondent No. 1 stated in its written statement that unless and until it is proved that the alleged offending vehicle was having a valid fitness certificate and permit to ply the said vehicle, no liability can be imposed upon the answering respondent. 15. It is also stated by Respondent No. 1 that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving license required as per Motor Vehicle Act, hence the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation. 16. Rest of the contents of claim petition were also denied but it was admitted that the vehicle was insured on the date of accident by the answering respondent. 17. No written statement was filed by Respondent No. 2 and 3. 18. From the pleadings of parties, following issues were framed: i. ....... OPP. ii. ......... OPP. iii. Relief. 19. Claimant entered in the witness box as PW1 and stated similar facts in his evidence by way of affidavit relating to sequence of events leading to the accident as were already stated by him in his claim petition. Medical Examination Report prepared at Civil Hospital was proved as Ex. PW1/A. Certified copy of FIR was proved as Ex. PW1/B. Chart showing difference in pay of a Junior Warrant Officer was proved as Ex. PW1/C. Pay slip of the claimant for the month of October, 2008 was proved as Ex. PW1/D. Secondary School Examination, 1986 certificate of the claimant was proved as Ex. PW1/E. Certified copy of chargesheet was proved as Ex. PW1/F. Air ticket purchased by Shri Daya Ram Yadav, Shri Dalipdara Yadav and Ms. Anjana Yadav from Jet Airways and Air Sahara respectively were proved as Ex. PW1/G. Advertisement of Air Force for the post of Airman was proved as Ex. PW1/H. Form54 filed by the Officerin Charge of Police Station Darrang, Assam with regard to the accident was proved as Ex. PW1/I. Disability certificate given by Medical Officer Shri Raja Ram Yadav vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 7 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54118099/ 3 at Rajasthan was proved as Ex. PW1/J. 20. In crossexamination by counsel for the Insurance Company, PW1 deposed that he is still doing job in Indian Air Force and he has no documentary evidence to show that he was entitled for promotion. He also deposed that he has not filed any ACR on record. He deposed that in the accident, he had lost all the documents and has nothing to show that he was pursuing MBA from IGNOU. He deposed that he remained hospitalized for nine months due to accidental injuries and had to set his children transferred from Kendriya Vidyalaya School at Tejpur and had to get them admitted in Narnaul, Haryana and it burdened him with additional cost of Rs.2,000/ per month. 21. Other suggestions contrary to his case were denied by him. 22. No other witness was examined by the claimant. 23. Insurance company examined its Dy. Manager, Shri Prem Singh as R1W1 who stated in his evidence by way of affidavit that counsel for the Insurance Company had sent a notice to the driver and owner of the offending vehicle at their correct addresses for production of original insurance policy, permit, fitness of the offending vehicle and driving license of the driver at the time of accident. He stated that those notices were not returned back undelivered and therefore same were deemed to be served. The notices were exhibited as Ex. R3W1/1, the postal receipts as per which these notices were sent were proved as Ex. R3W1/23 and the copy of insurance policy was proved as Ex. R3W1/4. 24. R3W1 further stated that the Insurance Company had assigned the job to Auto Risk Management Services Pvt. Ltd. for verification of driving license of the driver, permit and fitness certificate of the vehicle bearing No. AS123611 from RTO, Tejpur, Assam. As per report given by the surveyor, he could not verify anything as the authorized representative was told every time that the office has shifted to new premises, therefore, they could not locate the documents. The report of the surveyor was proved as Ex.R3W1/5. 25. R3W1 stated that as the driver was not having a valid driving license and vehicle was being plied without permit and fitness, Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify the insured. 26. No other witness was examined by Respondent No. 1 and no witness was examined by Respondent No. 2 and 3. 27. On 18.12.2012, P.E. was closed. Thereafter, none appeared for the claimant on 05.02.2013, 05.03.2013, 19.03.2013, 07.05.2013, 09.07.2013, 16.07.2013 and 24.07.2013 when it was noticed that the evidence of employer may have helped the claimant in receiving higher compensation. Court Notice was issued to the counsel for the claimant as well as to the claimant. Directions were also given to the claimant to get himself examined by a Medical Board of DDU Hospital for assessing physical disability suffered by him due to accidental injuries. Shri Raja Ram Yadav vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 7 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54118099/ 4 28. However, in spite of service of Court Notice, the counsel for the claimant did not appear in the Court to assist the Tribunal in arriving at just compensation and court notice could not be served upon the claimant as the report came that he has changed his government quarter and his fresh address is not known. 29. Therefore, this Tribunal was constrained to take up this claim petition for passing the award on the basis of evidence available on record.
texts.arguments: In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Gawhati High Court has observed as under: "In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case. In a criminal case in order to have conviction, the matter is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt and in a civil case the matter is to be decided on the basis of preponderance of evidence, but in a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal the standard of proof is much Shri Raja Ram Yadav vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 7 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54118099/ 5 below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in a civil case. But the tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt the nicety of a civil or of a criminal case. After all, it is a summary inquiry and this is a legislation for the welfare of the society" 40. In the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. MAC APP. No. 375/06 dated 05.07.12, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held as under: "8. In Bimla Devi and Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors., (2009) 13 SC 530, the Supreme Court held that in a petition under Section 166 of the Act, the Claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition under the Motor Vehicles Act. Para 15 of the report is extracted hereunder: "15. In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter. It was to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants. The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability. The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied." 9. The report in Bimla Devi (Supra) was relied on by the Supreme Court in its latest judgments in Parmeshwari v. Amir Chand (2011) 11 SCC 635 and Kusum Lata v. Satbir, (2011) 3 SCC 646." 41. In the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pushpa Rana & Ors.: 2009 ACJ 287, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that: "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondentsclaimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal (Supra). On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in F.I.R No. 955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle; (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of chargesheet under Sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of F.I.R., wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased. These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. Proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard. There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of the driver." 42. This case was noticed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case titled as Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh: 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310 where adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement. It was noted that there is nothing on record to show that the claimant had any enmity with the driver of offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in the case. Shri Raja Ram Yadav vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 7 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54118099/ 6 43. Therefore, this issue is decided in favour of claimant and against the respondents. ISSUE NO. 2: 44. In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., MANU/SC/1018/2010, Civil Appeal No. 8981/2010 decided on 18.10.2010, following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims: i. The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner. ii. Compensation payable in injury cases is payable under two heads. They are pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages. Pecuniary damages have three sub heads which are : (i) expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) (a) Loss of earning ( and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising of loss of earning during the period of treatment and (b) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (iii) Future medical expenses. Nonpecuniary damages (General Damage) are (iv) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries (v) loss of amenities (and /or loss of prospects of marriage) and (vi) loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). iii. 46. In the case of DTC v. Suraj Bhan, MAC APP. No. 196/07 dated 29.01.10 where judgment in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. v. Vijay Kumar Mittal (2008) ACJ 1300 was followed, in case of amputation of limb, non pecuniary compensation of Rs. 3 lacs was awarded. Rs. 1 lac was awarded for pain and suffering, Rs. 1 lac for loss of amenities of life and Rs. 1 lac for loss due to disfigurement. Shri Raja Ram Yadav vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 7 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54118099/ 7 47. In the case of Vijay Kumar Mittal (supra), the findings of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 17 are as under: "17. From the afore noted judicial decisions, a trend which emerges is that between the years 1985 and 1990, the courts have been awarding about Rs. 3 lacs under the head 'Non Pecuniary Damages' for amputation of leg resulting in permanent disability of 50% and above." 48. Therefore, this claimant is also awarded a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/ for Pain and Suffering, Rs. 1,00,000/ for Loss of Amenities of Life and Rs. 1,00,000/ for Loss Due to Disfigurement. 49. Since the claimant is provided with an artificial limb i.e. prosthesis device by Army Hospital, no compensation is awarded in favour of the claimant for artificial leg. 50. There is no evidence of cost of treatment or for purchase of medicines. 54. Therefore, he is awarded a compensation of Rs. 1,40,000/ for Loss of Leave for a period of seven months. 56. In Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. v. Lalita: AIR 1981 Delhi 558, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that there cannot be any deduction if domestic help is obtained from a family member. The Hon'ble High Court had observed as under: "........... A wrong doer cannot take advantage of this 'domestic element'. If the mother renders service to her, instead of a nurse, it is right and just that she should recover compensation for the value of the services that the mother has rendered to her. Mother's services were necessitated by the wrong doing and the injured should be compensated for it. (Cunnigharn v. Harrison 3 All E.R. 463) The services of a wife and mother are worth more than those of a housekeeper because she is in constant attendance and does many more things than a housekeeper. (Regan v. Williamson (1976) 2 All E.R. 241)." 57. This judgment was again quoted with approval by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Narayan Bahadur v. Sumeet Gupta and Anr., MAC APP. No. 762/11 dated 04.07.12. Shri Raja Ram Yadav vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 7 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54118099/ 8 58. Therefore, even if the claimant was being attended by his family members even then he is entitled to compensation for attendant's charges for seven months. 59. For deciding compensation payable to the claimant for attendant's charges, reliance is placed on minimum wages payable to an unskilled workman which at the time of accident were Rs. 3,271/ per month. 60. Therefore, the claimant is awarded a compensation of Rs. 22,897/ (Rs.3,271/ x 7) for Attendant's Charges. 61. The claimant has suffered amputation of right leg resulting in permanent disability. For calculating loss of future prospects, reliance is placed on National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Rajbir Singh & Ors., 2012 ACJ 1826. Since claimant's salary was Rs. 20,000/ per month at the time of accident, adding 50% towards future prospects, his assumed income will be Rs. 30,000/ per month. 63. Since he has suffered 40% disability and he was a Sergeant in Indian Air Force which needs full fitness, financial loss for the claimant will be at least 20% of the assumed income i.e. Rs. 6,000/ per month or Rs. 72,000/ per annum. 64. Since claimant was 38 years of age at the time of accident, applying multiplier of 15, loss of future prospects a sum of Rs. 10,80,000/ is awarded towards loss of future prospects. For this, reliance can be placed on the judgment passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Bajaj Allianze General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Bhikhari Yadav in MAC APP. No. 727/11 dated 03.01.12 as well as the New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Geeta & Ors. In the case of Bhikhari Yadav (Supra), the Hon'ble High Court had held that 'It is settled that in order to avoid the liability, the onus is on the insurance company to prove that there is breach of the policy conditions by the insured. The breach committed by the insured must be willful, e.g. where the insured entrusts a vehicle to a duly licensed driver and it is unlawfully driven by any other person not holding a valid and effective driving license, it cannot be said that the owner is guilty of willful breach. Similarly, where a vehicle is stolen by a thief holding no license and meets with an accident, it cannot be said that the insured is guilty of a willful breach.
